operative_context: System must distinguish between different semantic categories of item non-availability (e.g., deleted/operationally invalid vs. temporarily blocked/maintenance vs. manual restrictions)
Availability state semantics must separate maintenance periods from other forms of temporary unavailability in both backend logic and user-facing responses
Availability query results must clearly differentiate between items that are permanently non-rentable (deleted/invalid) and items that are temporarily unavailable
## 4.2.2 The system shall return availability status indicating whether the item is available or unavailable for the requested period.
Item availability status must reflect whether an item is recoverable (temporarily unavailable) or permanently non-rentable (operationally invalid)
exceptions: Maintenance periods block rental activity and mark items non-rentable, but may require distinct semantic representation from other non-rentable states
Manual availability restrictions take precedence over otherwise rentable time windows and must be semantically distinguishable from lifecycle-driven unavailability
Deleted items or items with invalid operational status must not be surfaced through the same availability wording as temporarily blocked items
conflicts_or_obsolete: Current implementation conflates operationally invalid records with temporarily unavailable items in availability query results (E5, E6, E10)
Existing non-rentable status handling does not distinguish maintenance-related periods from other forms of temporary unavailability (E6)
